# JSON-LD

*Standard*

The JSON-based format for structured data that Google recommends.

**Glossary** (*JSON-LD*): The structured data syntax Google recommends: one contiguous block that is easier to write correctly. Microdata and RDFa are interpreted the same way.

Narrative: the topic [Implementing structured data](../topics/structured-data-implementation.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

12 claims mention it: 10 shown or said at the event (2 not in Google docs, 4 confirmed by Google docs, 3 consistent with Google docs, 1 nothing to verify), 2 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data).

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C289`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, not in Google docs: A community speaker said a third-party study from early 2026 found that websites with JSON-LD were shown much more often, and that the industry reacted by adding schema markup everywhere. `[D1-C289, stage, Thiago Pojda, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C496`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Microdata has an advantage when payload size matters: embedded in the existing HTML, it avoids duplicating the page content in a separate JSON-LD block. `[D2-C496, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C495`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Google recommends JSON-LD because it is one contiguous block that is easier to author, so people make fewer mistakes with it. `[D2-C495, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C324`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Rich results differ from other search features because Google builds them from extra data that site owners provide, usually structured data and usually in JSON-LD format. `[D3-C324, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C334`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Slide, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google's Article slide showed the NewsArticle JSON-LD example from Google's Article documentation: a block in the page head with headline, three image URLs (1x1, 4x3 and 16x9), datePublished and dateModified with time zone offsets, and an author list of Person objects with name and url. `[D3-C334, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C383`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: In product markup, an offer's shipping and return information can point through a JSON-LD identifier (@id) to shipping and return data defined elsewhere. `[D3-C383, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D2-C446`](../sessions/D2-S11-finding-the-gold-nuggets-structured-data-media-and-more.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: The 'gold nuggets' that Google's feature extraction step pulls out of a page's HTML are structured data (such as JSON-LD), images and videos. `[D2-C446, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C494`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Google accepts three structured data syntaxes, JSON-LD, microdata and RDFa, which are all valid and are extracted at the very start into the same pipelines, so they are interpreted identically downstream. `[D2-C494, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C551`](../sessions/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Google strongly suggests describing a video's metadata with JSON-LD structured data, on top of placing the video in an HTML element on the page. `[D2-C551, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D1-C250`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: In a community demo, a fix loop gave a large LLM (Claude Opus) the current markup, the errors Google's test reported and Google's documentation, had it write new JSON-LD and re-ran the test, with at most three attempts; the demo's page passed on the second. `[D1-C250, stage, a community speaker, Day 1]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D1-C269`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Analysis: Author's view: an LLM fix loop that stops when Google's test passes proves only that the JSON-LD is valid, not that its values are true; Google's generative AI content guidance asks for AI-generated structured data to be fact-checked as well as validated. `[D1-C269, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C497`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Analysis: Default to JSON-LD and switch to microdata only where page weight is critical, since Google interprets all three syntaxes identically and JSON-LD is the one people get wrong least often. `[D2-C497, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-PRF-04` **SHOULD** · Documented: Keep each HTML response well under 2 MB and put the main content and JSON-LD early (its own text names it)
- `DEV-SDA-01` **SHOULD** · Documented: Write structured data as JSON-LD by default (4 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-VID-03` **SHOULD** · Documented: Describe videos with VideoObject markup and mark key moments with Clip or SeekToAction (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
